_help: Descriptions for the Flight configs panel (SPEC-70 DEV-030). Keys are FlightConfig field names. Fields: label, what, lower, higher, and optional slider [min, max] or [min, max, "log"] when the field's full range is too wide for a slider. Edits here need only a browser refresh. The values themselves come from the game; edits on the page last until you leave Play.

groups.name: Core assist (help every ship gets, whatever its thrusters)
Pushes (knockback and drift from hits and hazards)

MaxForwardSpeed.label: Max forward speed
MaxForwardSpeed.what: The fastest a ship flies forward without boost. Reverse and strafe speeds are fractions of it, and cruise starts from it.
MaxForwardSpeed.lower: every ship is slower in every direction
MaxForwardSpeed.higher: every ship is faster in every direction

ReverseSpeedFraction.label: Reverse speed
ReverseSpeedFraction.what: How fast you can back up, as a share of max forward speed.
ReverseSpeedFraction.lower: backing up is slow; 0 means you cannot reverse at all
ReverseSpeedFraction.higher: backing up gets closer to forward speed; 1 means just as fast

StrafeSpeedFraction.label: Strafe speed
StrafeSpeedFraction.what: How fast you can slide sideways, as a share of max forward speed.
StrafeSpeedFraction.higher: sideways movement is as quick as flying forward

BoostSpeedMultiplier.label: Boost top speed
BoostSpeedMultiplier.what: Boost multiplies the forward speed limit by this. It only raises forward speed, not reverse or strafe.
BoostSpeedMultiplier.lower: boost barely raises top speed; 1 means no higher top speed at all
BoostSpeedMultiplier.higher: boost lets you fly much faster than normal

BoostThrottle.label: Boost push
BoostThrottle.what: How hard thrusters may push while boosting, compared with normal full throttle. A ship's own thruster setting can override it.
BoostThrottle.lower: boost speeds you up gently; 1 means no extra push
BoostThrottle.higher: boost kicks in hard and reaches its top speed sooner, with longer plumes

ShieldSpeedFraction.label: Speed with shield up
ShieldSpeedFraction.what: While a ship's shield is up, its speed limits are multiplied by this: the shield's trade-off.
ShieldSpeedFraction.lower: raising the shield slows you a lot
ShieldSpeedFraction.higher: the shield costs little speed; 1 means no slowdown

MaxYawRateDeg.label: Max turn rate
MaxYawRateDeg.what: The fastest a ship may spin, in degrees per second. A heavy ship with weak thrusters may never reach it.
MaxYawRateDeg.lower: turning is capped slower, even for agile ships
MaxYawRateDeg.higher: agile ships can whip around faster

LinearAssistGain.label: Movement assist strength
LinearAssistGain.what: How much of the gap between your speed and the speed you are asking for the flight assist closes each tick, within what the thrusters can push.
LinearAssistGain.lower: softer, floatier: the ship eases toward the speed you want
LinearAssistGain.higher: snappier: the ship locks onto the speed you want almost at once

AngularAssistGain.label: Turning assist strength
AngularAssistGain.what: The same as movement assist, for spinning: how quickly the assist matches the turn rate you are asking for.
AngularAssistGain.lower: turns ease in and out, with a little drift

CoastDeceleration.label: Coast slowdown
CoastDeceleration.what: With no forward or back input, how quickly the ship slows down by itself, per second, as far as its thrusters allow.
CoastDeceleration.lower: you coast a long way after letting go; 0 means you keep your speed
CoastDeceleration.higher: the ship stops soon after you let go

CoreLinearAccel.label: Core push
CoreLinearAccel.what: Extra acceleration the ship core adds along every direction, on top of real thrusters, so ships with few or lopsided thrusters can still move.
CoreLinearAccel.lower: movement depends more on where thrusters are placed; 0 means thrusters only
CoreLinearAccel.higher: every ship accelerates, brakes and strafes harder whatever its layout

CoreMaxLinearForce.label: Core push limit
CoreMaxLinearForce.what: A cap on the core push force, so it matters less for heavy ships.
CoreMaxLinearForce.lower: big ships get little core help and rely on their thrusters
CoreMaxLinearForce.higher: big ships get the full core push too

CoreYawAccelDeg.label: Core turning
CoreYawAccelDeg.what: Extra turning acceleration from the ship core's gyro, on top of thrusters.
CoreYawAccelDeg.lower: turning depends more on thruster placement; 0 means thrusters only
CoreYawAccelDeg.higher: every ship starts and stops turning faster

CoreMaxYawTorque.label: Core turning limit
CoreMaxYawTorque.what: A cap on the gyro's turning force, so heavy ships turn on their thrusters more.
CoreMaxYawTorque.lower: big ships turn sluggishly unless they have good thrusters
CoreMaxYawTorque.higher: big ships get the full gyro help

CarryDecel.label: Push fade
CarryDecel.what: When a hit or hazard shoves the ship, how fast that drift fades away, in m/s every second.
CarryDecel.lower: shoves keep you drifting for a long time
CarryDecel.higher: shoves fade almost at once; 1,000,000 means the assist cancels them instantly

CarryBrakeDecel.label: Push fade while braking
CarryBrakeDecel.what: The same as push fade, while Brake is held.
CarryBrakeDecel.lower: braking does little against a shove

CarryYawDecel.label: Spin fade
CarryYawDecel.what: How fast a spin from a hit or hazard fades.
CarryYawDecel.lower: you keep spinning after a hit
CarryYawDecel.higher: spins from hits stop almost at once

MaxCarry.label: Max push speed
MaxCarry.what: The fastest a shove can make you drift, per direction.
MaxCarry.lower: big hits push you only a little
MaxCarry.higher: big hits can fling you across the map

MaxCarryYaw.label: Max push spin
MaxCarryYaw.what: The fastest a hit can spin you, in radians per second (3.5 is about 200°/s).
MaxCarryYaw.higher: hits can send you spinning wildly

TorqueWeight.label: Turning priority
TorqueWeight.what: When thrusters cannot do everything at once, how much the solver favours turning over moving.
TorqueWeight.lower: the ship keeps its speed but turns late
TorqueWeight.higher: the ship holds its heading but loses speed while turning

AllocationSweeps.label: Solver passes
AllocationSweeps.what: How many passes the solver makes to share the work between thrusters each tick. Rarely felt.
AllocationSweeps.lower: cheaper, but thrusters are used less precisely
AllocationSweeps.higher: thrusters are used more precisely, at a small CPU cost

ThrottleEpsilon.label: Throttle dead zone
ThrottleEpsilon.what: Thruster throttles below this count as off.
ThrottleEpsilon.lower: tiny corrections fire, so plumes may flicker
ThrottleEpsilon.higher: small corrections are dropped, so fine adjustments are lost

PlaneCorrection.label: Plane pull
PlaneCorrection.what: How much of the ship's drift off the flight plane is pulled back each tick.
PlaneCorrection.lower: after hits the ship may bob above or below the plane for a while
PlaneCorrection.higher: the ship snaps straight back onto the plane

IntensityRise.label: Plume rise
IntensityRise.what: Looks only: how quickly thruster plumes brighten when throttle goes up.

IntensityFall.label: Plume fade
IntensityFall.what: Looks only: how quickly thruster plumes dim when throttle goes down.
IntensityFall.lower: plumes linger after you let go
